title: VM 106 (palworld-server): take its address from the router (DHCP) so the router app can reserve it
description:
Learned on ADD4 (2026-10-10): the operator's Spectrum router app only lets a device be reserved — and so port-forwarded — when the router itself leased its address; a device with a fixed address shows no IP and Reserve is disabled. VM 106 has a fixed 192.168.1.106 set inside the guest (/etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml: `addresses: [192.168.1.106/24]`, default route via 192.168.1.1, nameserver 192.168.1.1), so ADD152's reservation cannot be made.

Inside VM 106 (it has the QEMU guest agent; reach it with `qm guest exec 106`): back up /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml, then make eth0 take its address by DHCP — `dhcp4: true` in place of the `addresses` and `routes` entries — keeping the `match` on macaddress bc:24:11:e8:9f:7a, `set-name: eth0` and the nameserver 192.168.1.1. Apply it with `netplan apply`.

Done when `qm guest exec 106 -- ip -4 addr show eth0` shows an inet address with `dynamic` (a lease from the router).
